rows.requirement: Identity linking uses OAuth 2.0 for authorization (the 'v1 auth mechanism' framing was dropped; direct OAuth 2.0 against the business domain via Discovery is always available, with the Accelerated IdP Flow as an additional OAuth-based fast path).
rows.quote:
**This specification uses
[OAuth 2.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749){ target="_blank" }**
for authorization.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md. OLD (04-08): "This specification uses OAuth 2.0 as the v1 auth mechanism. The schema is designed for incremental extension: future versions will add delegated identity provider support and non-OAuth authentication mechanisms..." NEW (08-25): "This specification uses OAuth 2.0 for authorization. Direct OAuth 2.0 against the business domain (via Discovery) is always available. When the business declares trusted external identity providers in config.providers, platforms MAY instead chain identity from a provider via the Accelerated IdP Flow, skipping the browser-based flow when they already hold a suitable upstream token." The 'v1 auth mechanism' / future-version framing is gone: config.providers and the Accelerated IdP Flow (JWT bearer assertion chaining, RFC 8693/7523) are now a SHIPPED feature in this version, not a placeholder (see IDL-056/IDL-057). Capability dev.ucp.common.identity_linking. Identity-linking existed in 2026-01-23 but 04-08 reworked it to capability-driven scopes / RFC 8414 discovery. Converted from needs-oauth 2026-07-03: the OAuth harness (checks/oauth_harness.py) drives the authorization-code+PKCE flow as the platform; graded in merchant_checks_04_08_oauth.py.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST authenticate token-endpoint requests using a method advertised in the business's token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported metadata.
rows.quote:
**MUST** authenticate token endpoint requests using a method advertised in
    the business's `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` metadata
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. RFC 8414 metadata field. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Token-endpoint auth method selection is the platform's request behavior. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Confidential clients SHOULD prefer asymmetric token-endpoint auth methods (private_key_jwt or tls_client_auth) and MAY use client_secret_basic where supported.
rows.quote:
**Confidential clients** (server-side platforms that can protect a
        credential) **SHOULD** prefer asymmetric methods —
        `private_key_jwt`
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. MAY client_secret_basic where business supports it. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Confidential-client method preference is the platform's choice. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Public clients MUST use token-endpoint auth method 'none' and rely on PKCE with S256 as proof-of-possession of the authorization code.
rows.quote:
**Public clients** (native, desktop, browser-extension, and on-device
        agent runtimes per
        [RFC 8252 §8.5](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-8.5){ target="_blank" })
        **MUST** use `none` and rely on PKCE with `S256`
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Capability-driven OAuth model new in 04-08 rework. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Public-client method choice + PKCE use are the platform's request behavior. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Public clients MUST NOT embed a client_secret.
rows.quote:
Public clients
        **MUST NOT** embed a `client_secret`.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Mirrored at Security Considerations L971-983 (was L581). Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Not embedding a client_secret is a property of the platform's distributed binary. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST select the strongest token-endpoint auth method offered by the business compatible with the platform's deployment model.
rows.quote:
Platforms **MUST** select the strongest method offered by the business
    that is compatible with the platform's deployment model.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Method-strength selection is the platform's negotiation behavior. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST include user identity tokens in the HTTP Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.
rows.quote:
**MUST** include user identity tokens in the HTTP `Authorization` header
    using the Bearer scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. RFC 6750 §2.1. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). rows.requirement: Platforms MUST implement the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow as the account linking mechanism.

    as the account linking mechanism.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST use PKCE with code_challenge_method=S256 for all authorization code exchanges.
rows.quote:
**MUST** use PKCE
    ([RFC 7636](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636){ target="_blank" })
    with `code_challenge_method=S256` for all authorization code exchanges.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. PKCE S256 mandatory. PKCE use on the request side is the platform's; the business-side enforcement is IDL-019/023/036/049 (checked). Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST validate the iss parameter in the authorization response to prevent Mix-Up Attacks, verifying it matches the AS issuer URI; if it does not match they MUST abort and discard the authorization response.
rows.quote:
**MUST** validate the `iss` parameter in the authorization response
    ([RFC 9207](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9207){ target="_blank" })
    to prevent Mix-Up Attacks. The platform **MUST** verify that the `iss`
    value matches the authorization server's issuer URI ... If the values do not match, the platform **MUST**
    abort and discard the authorization response.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Mix-up defense. Issuer declared in RFC 8414 metadata. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). iss validation is the platform's response handling; the business-side iss emission is IDL-018 (checked). Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: Platforms SHOULD include a unique unguessable state parameter in the authorization request to prevent CSRF.

rows.requirement: Businesses MUST validate user identity tokens on every user-authenticated request (iss, aud, exp, scopes, and client_id/azp).
rows.quote:
**MUST** validate user identity tokens on every user-authenticated request:
    verify `iss`, `aud` (the business's resource server identifier), `exp`,
    scopes, and `client_id` / `azp` (or equivalent) to confirm the token was
    issued to the authenticated platform client
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. RFC 9068 §4. Converted from needs-oauth 2026-07-03: the OAuth harness (checks/oauth_harness.py) drives the authorization-code+PKCE flow as the platform; graded in merchant_checks_04_08_oauth.py. Graded on its observable core (W2-F5 bar met 2026-08-04): the mint hook now yields deterministic EXPIRED, REVOKED, and FOREIGN-CLIENT tokens — exp/revocation (identity.expired/revoked_token_rejected, cited IDL-042) plus the client_id/azp binding half (identity.foreign_client_token_rejected, cited HERE) must each draw the invalid_token challenge. Whether an opaque-token business literally inspects iss/aud strings remains not black-box distinguishable; exp + revocation + client binding are the enforceable core the quote names.

rows.requirement: Businesses MUST emit a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge on 401 Unauthorized (identity_required) and 403 Forbidden (insufficient_scope) responses to user-authenticated operations.

**MUST** emit a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge per
    [RFC 6750 §3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-3){ target="_blank" }
    on `401 Unauthorized` (`identity_required`) and `403 Forbidden`
    (`insufficient_scope`) responses to user-authenticated operations.

rows.requirement: Businesses SHOULD publish protected resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and reference it via the resource_metadata parameter in WWW-Authenticate challenges; this becomes a MUST when the authorization server does not live on the business domain.
rows.quote:
**SHOULD** publish protected resource metadata at
    `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`
    ([RFC 9728](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728){ target="_blank" })
    and reference it via the `resource_metadata` parameter in
    `WWW-Authenticate` challenges. ... The business **MUST** publish this metadata when
    the authorization server does not live on the business domain.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md. OLD (04-08): "...This lets platforms discover the authorization server protecting the resource without relying on domain conventions and prepares the deployment for future delegated IdP scenarios where the AS may not live on the business domain." (SHOULD only, no explicit MUST condition). NEW (08-25): "...and prepares the deployment for future delegated domain conventions. The business **MUST** publish this metadata when the authorization server does not live on the business domain." A new conditional MUST was added: publishing protected-resource metadata is no longer purely a SHOULD once the AS is off-domain — it becomes obligatory, consistent with the new Discovery Step 1 (protected-resource-metadata-driven issuer resolution) which now formally allows the AS to live on a different origin.

rows.requirement: On RFC 8414 discovery, any non-2xx response other than 404 (network error or timeout) MUST abort and MUST NOT proceed to OIDC fallback.
rows.quote:
Any other non-2xx response, network error, or timeout: **MUST**
      abort. **MUST NOT** proceed to step 2.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); this exact clause's wording is unchanged, though it now sits inside a 3-step Discovery pipeline (a new Step 1 — protected-resource-metadata issuer resolution — precedes what was 'step 1' in 04-08; this RFC 8414 fetch is now sub-item 1 of the pipeline's Step 2). See IDL-033 for the issuer-comparison clause that DID change substance. Strict two-tier discovery hierarchy; RFC 8414 primary.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST NOT silently fall through on any error other than 404 in RFC 8414 discovery.
rows.quote:
Platforms **MUST NOT** silently fall through on any error other than
`404` in step 1.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged (same reorg context as IDL-031).

rows.requirement: The issuer value in discovered metadata MUST byte-for-byte match the AS issuer resolved in Discovery Step 1 (which may now be a different origin than the business domain, via protected-resource metadata); platforms MUST NOT normalize before comparison.
rows.quote:
The `issuer` value in the discovered
metadata **MUST** byte-for-byte match the AS issuer selected in Step 1
(per
[RFC 8414 §3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414#section-3.3){ target="_blank" }).
Platforms **MUST NOT** normalize (e.g., strip trailing slashes) before
comparison.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md. OLD (04-08): "The issuer value in the discovered metadata MUST match the discovery base URI exactly (per RFC 8414 §3.3). ... the value must be a byte-for-byte match." where 'discovery base URI' was ALWAYS the business's own domain (a flat two-tier hierarchy). NEW (08-25): "The issuer value in the discovered metadata MUST byte-for-byte match the AS issuer selected in Step 1 (per RFC 8414 §3.3)." Discovery is now a 3-step pipeline: a new Step 1 resolves the AS issuer via RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, and that issuer MAY be hosted on a different origin than the business domain (defaulting to the business domain only when no protected-resource metadata is published). The comparison target for byte-for-byte matching therefore changed from 'always the business domain' to 'whatever Step 1 resolved,' a genuine scope broadening, not just a rename. RFC 8414 §3.3. Converted from needs-oauth 2026-07-03: the OAuth harness (checks/oauth_harness.py) drives the authorization-code+PKCE flow as the platform; graded in merchant_checks_04_08_oauth.py. Business half graded (metadata issuer == discovery base, byte-for-byte); the 'platforms MUST NOT normalize' half is platform-bound.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST request only the derived scope set (from config.scopes) and not a superset.
rows.quote: Platforms **MUST** request only the derived scope set — not a superset.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Derived from business config.scopes. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). Requesting only the derived scope set is the platform's request authoring. Platform-conformance exemption candidate.

rows.requirement: On the authorization response, the platform MUST verify state matches the sent value and iss matches the discovered issuer URI; if either fails it MUST discard the response.
rows.quote:
the platform **MUST** verify that the `state`
parameter matches the value sent in step 2, and that the `iss` parameter
matches the authorization server's `issuer` URI from discovered metadata.
If either check fails, the platform **MUST** discard the authorization
response.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. Reclassified manual 2026-07-03: binds the PLATFORM (request author), not the business — no merchant check can grade it (suite requester-bound policy; CAT-034 precedent). state/iss verification is the platform's response handling. Platform-conformance exemption candidate. This is the Account Linking Flow's own local 'Step 3', unaffected by the separate Discovery-section Step 1/2/3 renumbering (see IDL-033).

rows.requirement: The token-request code_verifier MUST correspond to the code_challenge sent in the authorization request; businesses MUST reject token requests where code_verifier is absent or does not verify.
rows.quote:
The `code_verifier` **MUST** correspond to the
`code_challenge` sent in step 2. Businesses **MUST** reject token requests
where `code_verifier` is absent or does not verify against the stored
`code_challenge`.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (was identity-linking.md); wording unchanged. rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (Future Extensibility section) -> now split across the 'For Platforms' guidelines and the new 'Identity Providers' section. OLD (04-08, Future Extensibility): "When `config.providers` is present, the platform uses the provider selection and identity chaining flows defined in that version. When `config.providers` is absent (as in v1), platforms **MUST** fall back to direct OAuth 2.0 against the business domain via RFC 8414 discovery." — config.providers was an UNSHIPPED placeholder; the fallback was an explicit MUST. NEW (08-25): config.providers + the Accelerated IdP Flow are now a SHIPPED, real feature (see the 'provider' $def and config.providers property in source/schemas/common/identity_linking.json, and the new Identity Providers / Accelerated IdP Flow / IdP Requirements doc sections). [prior note retained]: config.providers is a reserved extension point in schema $comment (NOW REMOVED — see IDL-057). The v1 fallback is the platform's flow selection. **Forward-compatibility rule for platforms:** When `config` contains fields
not defined in this version of the spec, platforms **MUST** ignore those

rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (Future Extensibility section retained under the same heading, content changed). OLD (04-08): "When `config` contains fields not defined in this version of the spec (`providers` or any other future field), platforms **MUST** ignore those fields and proceed using OAuth 2.0 with RFC 8414 discovery on the business domain, as defined here. This ensures v1 platform implementations remain valid as the spec evolves." — ignoring unknown fields ALWAYS led to plain direct OAuth (because providers itself was always unknown/unshipped in v1). NEW (08-25): "...platforms **MUST** ignore those fields. Platforms **MUST** treat provider entries with an unsupported `type` as filtered out, then apply the rules in [Identity Providers](#identity-providers) to what remains." — because config.providers is now a real, parsed field, 'ignore unrecognized config fields' no longer implies 'always fall back to direct OAuth': a platform must additionally filter unsupported provider *entry types* and then apply the Identity Providers section's rules to the remainder, which may still yield Accelerated IdP chaining if a supported provider entry survives the filter. **OIDC Discovery (Fallback):** Fetch

notes: No official conformance oracle exists for identity-linking: .vendor/conformance contains only checkout/order/fulfillment/card-credential/webhook/etc. tests; grep found no identity-linking, oauth, or scope tests. All rows official_oracle=false.

2026-08-25 is the doc-reorg + provider-chaining release: docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (#723 hierarchy reorg). The identity-linking capability grew substantially: config.providers (a 'reserved extension point' in 04-08) is now a REAL, shipped feature (a new 'provider' $def in the schema, plus new doc sections Identity Providers / Accelerated IdP Flow / IdP Requirements) enabling JWT-bearer-assertion identity chaining (RFC 8693 token exchange + RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant) so platforms can skip the browser-based OAuth flow with a trusted upstream IdP. Discovery also gained a new leading step (RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata resolves the AS issuer, which MAY now be a different origin than the business domain) ahead of the previously-only two-tier RFC 8414/OIDC hierarchy. These are the two structural deltas driving this version's reworded rows (IDL-001, IDL-030, IDL-033, IDL-056, IDL-057, IDL-059, IDL-062). No row was found DEAD in 08-25.

Identity linking EXISTED in the 2026-01-23 version, but the 2026-04-08 version REWORKED it onto capability-driven scopes ({capability}:{scope}) and RFC 8414 authorization-server discovery. This is the spec-significant delta; flagged on rows IDL-001, IDL-016, IDL-029, IDL-037, IDL-059 in the 04-08 register.

Almost all normative rows are OAuth-flow obligations requiring a live authorization server / browser-driven consent, hence testability=needs-oauth or manual. The fetch-only obligations (RFC 8414 metadata presence: scopes_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported, code_challenge_methods_supported, authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, protected-resource metadata, well-known publication) are marked testable. TLS-1.2-minimum (IDL-053) is testable but not browser_capable (transport-level inspection).

schema_enforced=true only for real JSON-Schema constraints in identity_linking.json: scope_token regex pattern (IDL-037/IDL-059) and the required config/scopes structure (IDL-060). The scope-name pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ in prose (IDL-037) is a subset of the full schema scope_token pattern, which itself was BROADENED in 08-25 to allow hyphens (IDL-059, reworded).

Scope vocabulary referenced across rows: *.catalog.*:read, dev.ucp.shopping.checkout:manage, dev.ucp.shopping.order:read, dev.ucp.shopping.order:manage (well-known); businesses MAY declare custom scopes following the same {capability}:{scope} convention.

config.scopes (UCP hard gates: scopes that REQUIRE user auth) vs OAuth scopes_supported (accepted vocabulary the AS will honor) are distinct; their set difference is the optional/auth-unlocked layer (IDL-017, IDL-038, IDL-054).

Schema reorg note (source/schemas/common/identity_linking.json): the scope_policy.description $ref changed from '../shopping/types/description.json' to 'types/description.json' (a common/types/ relocation, per the harness-provided reorg map) — no existing row quotes that $ref, so no row was affected. The schema's top-level and config-level $comment fields (describing config.providers as a future reserved extension point) were REMOVED, consistent with providers now being a real, documented property.
